title: Skill eval run record
description: Shape of the run record SKILL.md's Procedure step 7 writes when a gate run completes: one record per run, written into the target repository's own eval-results location, never an edit to an earlier one. This file pins shape and carries each field's full rationale in its `description`s. What a run must capture is stated by that Procedure step, and the split is deliberate -- a corpus of records can validate individually against a schema and still drift into disagreeing key spellings and unreferenced attachments when no procedure ever says what to record. Additional keys are permitted: a run may carry its own extra context (a run-shape note, a pointer to a superseded record) without needing this schema widened, and a repository migrating pre-existing records onto this contract is doing its own work, not being retro-graded by this file.

date.description: The run's real calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD. Not a relative position in a git log, and not the date the record was tidied up.

issue.description: Full URL of the issue or change this run was performed for. A bare number is rejected by construction: it resolves only inside the repository that minted it, and a run record outlives that context.

commit.description: The exact commit the graded content was read at, as a hex object name. Without it a score cannot be re-derived, which is the whole point of recording one.

runner.description: The eval runner Procedure step 1 confirmed. Both fields are obtained firsthand in the environment the trials ran in -- never from memory or from a toolchain pin read elsewhere.

name.description: The runner's name as invoked (a binary name, or a repository-owned script path such as evals/scripts/gitapex_run_eval_suite.py).

version.description: For an external, independently-versioned binary, the version string it itself reported. For a version-controlled, repository-owned runner with no independent version identity, the hex commit that last touched its own content (obtained firsthand, e.g. `git log -1 --format=%H -- <runner path>`), never a version a requester reports, a toolchain manifest declares, or an earlier record carries. A run that could not obtain either is not recorded here; step 1 stops instead.

fixture_set.description: Which fixtures ran and where their definitions live, specific enough that a reader can open them. A count alone does not satisfy this.

trials_per_fixture.description: How many trials each fixture got. One is a legitimate answer and a disclosed limit; zero is not a run.

models.description: Alias -> full model ID, covering every model actually invoked. Keyed by whatever alias the run used, valued by the full current identifier: an alias can re-resolve to a different underlying model over time, and a record that stored only the alias silently changes meaning when it does.

dispatch_mechanism.description: How the run was isolated from the authoring context. Whether isolation was actually achieved is a claim this field records and a reviewer checks; the schema can only require that the claim be made.

scorer.description: What produced the numbers -- the grader, checker, or script, named precisely enough to re-run.

score_files.description: One entry per model actually run, each pointing at that model's own score file. Named for the pointers it holds rather than for the scores themselves, which live one level down in those files under their own `scores` key (see eval-scores.schema.json) -- two differently-shaped lists sharing one key name is exactly the drift this contract exists to stop. A model listed in `models` with no entry here has no results and must be disclosed in `known_gaps` rather than left implied.

model_id.description: The full model ID, matching a value in `models`.

file.description: Path to this model's score file, relative to this record. Every attachment a run produces is reachable from here; an unreferenced file next to a record is an orphan, not a result.

gate.description: The verdict this run produced and the comparison that produced it. A record holding candidate scores but no outcome cannot tell a later reader whether the edit was kept, which is the same re-derivability failure the runner-confirmation step stops a run for.

verdict.description: The gate's own two outcomes. There is no third: an ordinary tie is a REJECT, not an undecided state.

candidate_class.description: The class the candidate was declared as BEFORE scoring. Recorded because the two classes are graded by different rules, and because a class assigned after seeing the score is the failure the predeclaration requirement exists to prevent.

split.description: Which split the comparison ran over. Constant by construction rather than free text: a verdict computed over train or test is not this gate's verdict at all, and a free-text field would let such a run be recorded as one. Holding the value fixed makes an out-of-contract verdict unrecordable instead of merely visible, at the cost of a field that carries no information when the contract was followed -- the trade this repository's fail-closed default asks for.

prior_mean.description: The baseline this candidate was compared against, as a string at exactly the precision the scorer published it at. A string, not a number, because JSON number serialization drops trailing zeros and the gate compares at published precision -- a prior at any other precision is ambiguous input the gate fails loudly on rather than rounds. The pattern bounds the value to [0,1], the range the Precondition gate requires of any scorer, but deliberately fixes no number of decimals: six is this skill's own bundled scorer's published precision, not every scorer's, and pinning it here would invalidate a record produced by the test-pass or battle-test scorers the Precondition gate equally allows. That the two means share one precision is a rule the Gate step states and no JSON Schema can express across two fields.

candidate_mean.description: The candidate's own mean, at the same published precision as prior_mean and for the same reason.

prior_context_cost.description: The predeclared context-cost measure before the patch. Required for a pruning-only candidate, whose lexicographic exception turns on this number; meaningless for an ordinary one.

candidate_context_cost.description: The same measure after the patch. Required for a pruning-only candidate.

known_gaps.description: The run's disclosed scope limits. Never omit this key to mean 'none': a run with nothing to disclose says so with a single explicit 'none known' entry, so a silent omission can never read as a clean run.

headline_pattern.description: A one-paragraph statement of the run's main finding, for a reader who will not open the score files.

attempt.description: Optional, human-readable ordinal for a reader distinguishing runs that share the same date and commit -- convenience labeling only, not itself what prevents a collision (a small integer is exactly what two independent, uncoordinated invocations could both compute). The actual collision-avoidance mechanism is the record's own filename, which must carry a high-entropy random component each invocation generates independently (see SKILL.md step 7); this field may echo that value or a separately assigned sequence number for readability.

supersedes.description: Optional. When this record corrects an earlier one, the earlier record it replaces. A correction is a new record naming its predecessor, never an edit to it.
